decisions.text: arranged: columns by region: no comparison within a panel is stated (facts.compare): one series per panel, the most panels and the least clutter (13-15 DP-1); runner-up for review: series in each panel by region (D-38 (i))
categories sorted by their total over every panel, largest first, the same order in every panel (G2.1)
one colour for every mark: every variable is on the rows or columns (G7.50)
type bar: categories compared by value
one shared scale: one scale for every panel, so that sizes compare across panels (G7.48)
in a panel 114 pt wide: “Operations” and “HR” come within 10 pt of each other under vertical bars, with every multi-word name wrapped: horizontal bars, names right-aligned at the left
labels as a set, 1 decimals, bare numbers: 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5
digits hidden: millions, stated in the scale's title (R2-05, D-3): “Expenses ($ million)”
a horizontal scale: bare numbers, and its title centred below with the unit in parentheses: “Expenses ($ million)”
highlighted in the strong shade of their colour: HR; the others keep their colour
1 × 3 panels of equal size, abutting, divided by light separators, no box round a panel (G7.51); each 89 pt wide
the names once, at the left of the first column; the scale labels under the bottom row, its title once; column headers above the top row (G7.49)

findings.message: facts.compare not given: say which dims the insight compares directly, so that their series share a panel (G1.19)
findings.title: the series the insight compares directly share a panel

source.shows: the book's merged bars for several totals of which only some parts are shown: one panel per region, the departments once at the left, one shared scale repeated under each panel and titled once; not a stacked bar or pie, which would suggest all parts are shown (G1.42); the names do not fit under columns in panels this narrow, so the bars run horizontally; West's HR bar in the strong shade (a highlight named by panel and category)
